utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honour. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I put on the record first that Mr. Mladic is not present in court. Second, that the Chamber has received a form absence from court, it says due to illness but it is clear that Mr. Mladic, as is written down by the principal officer, that he doesn't come to court because of family visit and it's not due to illness, and that he waives his right to attend trial today and, as I do understand, most likely tomorrow as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll proceed in the absence of the accused. Since the accused is not there, the Chamber would prefer to have the usual schedule, which is sitting for one hour and a half, taking half an hour break, and then not -- one break less but longer breaks. If there are no preliminaries, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Turkusic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony and may also urge you to focus your answer on the questions that are put to you. Mr. Lukic, if you're ready, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Turkusic.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have 65 ter 10407 in e-court, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's P2043.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see that this is the document we discussed yesterday. Now, on page 5, there is a legend. Let's see that first. It would be good if we could have page 5 on the left side of the screen, and on the right side page 6 in B/C/S, because there is a sketch of the site on page 6. I know that this will be a bit difficult for those who don't understand B/C/S to follow, that's why I will read out what it says on the left-hand side. "FT 1, fixed point 1. FT 2, fixed point 2. S, north. 1, part of projectile. 2, place of impact. 3, water pump. 4, water containers. 5, blood traces. 6, tissue traces." And then there is a square with lines coming out of it, and it reads: "From 1 to 6 places where photographs were taken from." In this photograph, the arrow on the right-hand side, what does it represent? Is this the trajectory of the projectile?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what this sketch suggests. I didn't make the sketch but that's how I understand it, because in the same way, north is indicated, and this can be understood that this type of symbol is supposed to -- supposed to mean -- indicate a direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Our ballistics expert measured the angle between north and this arrow, and the angle is exactly 320 degrees.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the report does say that the azimuth is 320, so this measuring done by your experts is only a verification whether the direction was indicated here in a correct way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. We'll go into that later. Now, this sketch, when you lay this sketch over a map of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if I could ask for 1D1231 to be displayed from e-court. That's the document I wasn't ready to discuss yesterday. Can it be blown up a bit more? Some more, please. [In English] If we can zoom in one, a bit more, bit more. That's it, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes. Just before any questions about this map are put to the witness, would the Defence be so kind as to indicate all of the markings that are on the sketch; in particular, which were not on the original version of the sketch in case the witness may not remember all of the markings that were on the original sketch. And in particular I would note that the line attached to the arrow to the right of the sketch was -- appears to have been added by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, many things were added on this sketch, just for better understanding, and I will go through all of them step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This sketch has now been laid over a map of Sarajevo, and it was explained to me that the city map is oriented exactly toward geographical north, as can be -- which you can tell from the thin lines. It was also explained to me that 207 degrees, just as Judge Orie correctly understood yesterday, was a line, an oblique line, that was drawn and only represents an extension of that school wall. The vertical line going from north to south, that is the thin black line going through this image, is the north-south axis and it cuts through the Simon Bolivar school. The red line marked 1, which we also saw yesterday on that other map of Sarajevo, when we discussed the position of the wall of that school, represents the axis on which there is the school wall. As the OTP requested, this line marked 2 is the trajectory of the shell as entered in this sketch. The number 3 marks another arrow, and is -- and points south. We see that there is an angle of 63 degrees. That's the angle under which the shell -- that is the angle between the trajectory of the shell and the wall of the gym.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who says so?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what we measured. Of course, it wasn't me. I'm not an expert. Our ballistics experts did that. According to our measurements, if you add up 207 degrees, indicating the wall of the school, and 63 degrees, you get 270 degrees, which is pure west, whereas north, marked by an arrow, is, in fact, rotated by 50 degrees in relation to true north, which is marked here, you see that it says 50 degrees. Do you agree that this sketch is correctly laid on the map of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. But I think that the input is arbitrary because, after so much time, and given the fact that the wall was renovated, nobody can tell that the angle of descent was really 63 degrees. What kind of measurement could have produced such a result?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The measurement of the arrows on this sketch of the site about which we agreed that the angle between geographical north and the arrow indicating the impact was 320 degrees. Do you have any other information?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I object to the way this is being framed. The witness didn't agree that -- to the angles as you put them regarding the sketch. Witness agreed that he had assessed the azimuth as 320 degrees, which corresponded with what you represented to be the angle on the sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Prosecution has its own experts. They are invited to check if this angle is 320 in between of those two arrows. We claim it and we are certain in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Our problem is that you are testifying to what your expert has done. You're not using your experts to tell us, and you yourself have confessed not to be an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So we just don't even understand, at times, your reasoning as you go along. So -- and I'm just wondering --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's hard for me too --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm just wondering if you are actually allowed to be testifying as you have been doing this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour invited me to explain the markings on the map and I just complied with their request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And we will have of course our experts here to explain these markings, of course, during the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The key issue in the whole matter, Mr. Lukic, seems to be, and until now, the material has not been clear on that, is whether the wall, as it existed at the time, really is in the position as it is put on this map. That's the key issue in the whole matter. Apart from that, whether some angle is 63 degrees, take one simple thing and you can verify it. I mean, it's basic school -- elementary school technique, I would say, that at least what I learned that, not being an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We agree, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the key issue is was the wall where, it is suggested here it was at least the orientation of the wall, was it where it is said here, that's one. And then second, of course, whether the sketches made at the time are accurate, "yes" or "no." These are the vital elements to draw any conclusions. Ms. Harbour?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I agree with that. The issue of whether it's a simple issue of measuring degrees with a protractor, I would disagree that that's one of the key issues. In addition, I think the premise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not saying it is. I'm just saying that that's the easy part, not a vital part, but the simple part --

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- because everyone can check that within a second. The more -- the vital issues are: What is the orientation of the wall, and is the sketch and the underlying measurements, are they accurate "yes" or "no." That is in a nutshell what is important. And then every expert further can tell us everything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If the Prosecution is claiming that those markings are wrong, they should tell us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have not heard any such suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Me neither.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but as I said, there are two vital elements. The one is the orientation of the wall --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If the orientation of the wall is wrong, then we lose ground, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We admit that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the first -- that's the factual basis on which experts then can tell us what their opinion is but that factual basis should be there. Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: My only objection would be to suggesting to the witness that he agreed to something which he didn't. As long as we are sticking very closely to what the witness actually gave evidence about, I have no objection to pursuing this theory or testing this issue with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you could see, Your Honour, this is 65 ter number and 65 ter document of the Prosecution. We used their document. We used the markings made by somebody in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Two questions. Accuracy of the sketch, which is overlaid on this map, that's one. Second, whether it's accurately following the orientation of the wall. These are the two basic issues. If we have clear evidence on that, we can further ask evidence from whatever experts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked the witness, and he responded as accurately as he was able to. I think that I finished this topic and I would move on to something -- some other issues. If you have any additional questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I would have one additional question. In those reports, and I tried to understand them all in full detail, not much if anything is said about the origin of fire, as far as distance is concerned. Is that well understood? Or is there agreement among the parties? I mean, there was a suggestion that the direction is in the Nedzarici direction. Now if you draw a line to the Nedzarici direction between anything between 500 metres and 6 kilometres, you are on Federation-held territory, you're on Serb-held territory, you're on Federation-held territory, you're again on Serb-held territory, so if the parties agree that in this report nothing is said about the length of the trajectory then we can --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is the case, as we understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Harbour, do we agree that the distance on which the projectile travelled is not described or calculated anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: In these reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In these reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Although other evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's -- that's --

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: -- will be submitted. But in these reports we agree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we entirely focus here on the direction from which the fire came. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll skip some parts of your statement now, and we will move on to the shelling of -- known as Markale 2. The relevant paragraphs in your statement are 53 through?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the last paragraph number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the interpreters couldn't hear the last number you mentioned, 53.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How much time did you need, Mr. Turkusic, from the moment you learned of the explosion until you arrived at the site?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned of the explosion when I was on my way between our base and the explosion site. I was between these two points, and I saw cars from which body parts were sticking out because they were transporting the wounded and dead. We stayed there for a couple of minutes and it took us another five to ten minutes to get there. These are all rough estimates but given the length of time that elapsed, I believe that it's precise enough. It may have taken some 15 minutes from the moment of the explosion for the vehicles to be loaded with the wounded and dead and set off to the hospital. That would be a rough chronology of the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. That's what you said in your testimony in General Milosevic's trial 7, 8 to 10 minutes, that's how long it lasted, that's what you said, all of it?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean all of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From the moments when you found out and then returned to the scene, you said that 7, 8 or 10 minutes had elapsed. You said roughly.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly. Nobody used a stop watch to measure the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. What about traffic? Was it moving towards Bascarsija or towards Skenderija?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the west.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Is that the normal flow of traffic in that street?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. And that is the shortest route to the clinical centre, to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You remember that seriously wounded man who had a big hole in his body, who was transferred from there?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see that live. That photograph went all around the world but I saw it only later, from the photographs that were accessible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see, with the assistance of Ms. Stewart, V0004749-1-A? We need a still at 1 minute 48 seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This will be up momentarily. Ms. Stewart was not informed ahead of time, so it's just taking some moments to pull up the clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Our patience and Ms. Stewart's skills will resolve the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right. We'll go back to this, to give Ms. Stewart more time as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think she found it. Just be patient.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1:48.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We know now who we are speaking about, right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see blood underneath this man?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, underneath his right arm, you can see a pool of blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this photograph, could you please put a circle around the place where you see blood?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We first have -- we are watching a still of a video which -- we are watching a video and we have stopped it. So you need to first produce a still from this video so that we have a picture, a picture which can then be uploaded and can marked. But I'm afraid that we can't do it from this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will move on, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your view, how was this man wounded, with what?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we certainly see the same picture and below his right hand, the right-hand of the victim, we see a red pool and vertically upwards we can see this blood flowing across the shirt of that man, the sleeve of the shirt. So that is to say that is how the wound was inflicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I do apologise but are you saying that this wound was inflicted by this explosion of the mortar shell?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: The witness has already answered the question, but if we could have a foundation laid for the witness's knowledge of how wounds were inflicted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, are you asking the opinion of a lay person or are you -- what are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found in one place that the witness explained that these wounds were inflicted by shrapnel from a mortar shell, so I'm asking him whether that is his position today as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a well known fact that shrapnel because of their physical asymmetry during the impulse, during which they fly, they rotate irregularly, and very quickly, say like a helicopter propeller. If a rotating shrapnel the size of a cigarette enters a body, under a particular angle, then that would suffice. Then we see what we see now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this picture was the explosion on the left, right, top or bottom?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was behind the witness -- the victim's back.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that this victim was not registered among the victims of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first seek clarification of the previous answer? Behind the witness's back, what do you mean by that? Is that from the angle of view from the photographer? Is that at the opposite side of the road? Could you be a bit more precise and try to describe where the explosion was in relation to the position of the body of this man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can. This photograph suggests even 3D, so the place where the shell fell was to the left, behind the back of the victim as we see the victim, and at a place that the picture would have included had it gone a bit further left, we see in the upper left-hand corner part of the building of the Markale Market and around the middle of that building is the place where the shell fell, and that cannot be seen because it is a bit outside the frame of this photograph. That is to say on the other side of the street. But along the sidewalk on this street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, other side of the street next to the building of which we still see a small part at the left upper part of the photograph. Then I think your next question, Mr. Lukic, was whether this person, the wounded person we see hanging over this rail, whether that person was registered as a victim, and then the interpreters did not catch the last part of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was the gist of my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know whether this person was registered as one of the victims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the same video now, from 3 minutes 52 seconds to 4 minutes, 2 seconds?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back to 3:52 again?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we are going to see that first a soldier with a Kalashnikov is entering and he does not have his hood out, and after that another soldier appears without a Kalashnikov and without a hood pulled out of -- or with a hood. We can play the video now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A bit further, just -- that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this door, entrance door, do you see -- do you know whose headquarters were there, which BH Army unit?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. In paragraph 75 of your statement -- we are done with the video now. First you say that the fuse which is usually made of aluminium usually gets completely destroyed. The stabiliser at the other end of the shell was important. We have a video that was brought by Mr. Suljevic. You know who Mr. Suljevic is, don't you?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that video, we see two stabilisers registered and they're marked with numbers 12 and 13. Do you have an explanation, how come two stabilisers were there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: This question is completely lacking in foundation. There is a reference to a video brought by an individual and stabilisers that are numbered.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your witness brought that video.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it should be clearly put to the witness what the factual basis of your question is, not to say in a video it is shown that it was nice weather, can you tell us about the weather? Then either you ask a separate question or if you refer to any evidence you have to put that evidence to the witness in such a way that he's able to comment on the content of it, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First of all, I should ask him whether he knows whether there were two tail fins found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you can ask that without referring to Mr. Suljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: And in addition if specific parts of the record could be referenced for our benefit so that we can check this. If there are references to the transcript of Mr. Suljevic who didn't testify about Markale 2, particularly that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I shall continue and ask you whether you know that on the scene two stabilisers were found?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The question was if you know that two stabilisers were found at the site?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is the fourth time I'm giving evidence about this case, and I testified in much detail. This is the first time that two stabilisers are being mentioned. I've never heard of two stabilisers before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the simple answer is no, you're not aware of two stabilisers being found. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll get there yet. You said that you were not aware of it. In paragraph 79, you say: "After the meeting of the investigation team, we checked with the UN observers and they stated that there was no artillery activity from the ABiH territory." To the best of your knowledge, did the radars supposed to monitor artillery fire function at the time? Were they in operation?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was a radar controlling a certain area, but this shell could have bypassed the radar. It all depends upon the orientation of the radar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was not the question that was put to you. The question was whether you are aware of a radar and whether it was operational. That's the question. All the other questions will come later. Was there a radar and was it operational at the time of this shelling incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We only had unofficial information about the radar. Nobody ever informed us whether it was on, whether it was operational, and which area it covered. It was a secret to us basically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 102 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 102. You say, "I heard there was a radar that arrived to Sarajevo at the beginning of the war, but that it broke down very soon."

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was said on TV, our TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So can you say now what you think, whether the radar was operational or not?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My opinion is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can ask for facts the witness knows but whether in his opinion it did or not, the conclusions are there to be drawn by the Chamber. So factual basis for which would enable the Chamber to draw any conclusions from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The factual basis for my question is page 16, line 13, and paragraph 102 of witness's statement. Today he was explaining about the radar, it was operational, and in paragraph 102, he's claiming that that radar was not operational.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic I think this is not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You misread.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: He said: "We only had unofficial about the radar. Nobody ever informed us whether...," and so on. Your question is already answered in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then what is noted in paragraph 102 is not correct, in his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that is what he heard, no official information, and I think the witness said that he heard this on television which is not an official source of knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know that on that day, UNPROFOR radars were unable to observe fire from Serbian positions either?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave evidence about that in the previous case, and I gave explanations that I can repeat now. That radar can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, what we have is your statement. We have not read your previous testimony so there is no need to refer to that. The question was whether you are aware that radar systems were unable to detect Serbian fire -- an UNPROFOR radar, I should say. Please tell us. Apparently you have testified about it. Do it again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We learned that the UNPROFOR report states that on that day, there was no fire from the BH Army positions. Whether or not radars detected fire from Serbian positions, I think that they did not, but that doesn't mean that there wasn't any, because a radar has a certain orientation in space, so it can detect or not detect something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 103, you say, it was generally known -- it was common knowledge that the slopes of Mount Trebevic were occupied by the Serbian occupation forces.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say "occupation forces," what do you understand that to mean? What's an occupier?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When an army wages war in the territory of an internationally recognised country against its government, killing civilians, that is -- can be defined or that is defined as occupation. Our flag had been flying in front of the United Nations building in New York for four years.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that occupation presupposes a foreign armed force?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are irrelevant questions to deal with with this witness. It may be all relevant but what a police technician could tell us about legal opinions about occupation is not relevant at this moment. And apart from that, we all have heard many, many times that the views on who was the legal force and who was not a legal force differed quite a bit and it's not useful to deal with that with this or many of other witnesses. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I didn't want to enter the area of legal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed. You may proceed on questions of fact, and this is a question of opinion and expression of opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in your reports, you used terms such as "occupier," Chetnik, aggressor and so on, to denote the opposing Serbian side?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Show me report where I used the term "Chetnik," please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you use the term "aggressor"?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I did. That's a historical fact. It was proven before the international court that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to stop you there. When you used the word "occupying force," did you refer to the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that at that time, it was common, at least on your side, in military documents of the BH Army, to denote or to call the Serbian side as Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have the opportunity to see military reports, given my duties and my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This on-site investigation on the 28th of August, 1995, you did it in the presence of UNPROFOR personnel, right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was your task on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My task, and that of my colleagues who were there, was to determine the azimuth as precisely as possible, the direction from which the shell came, the angle of descent, and all other technical details, to give an accurate description of the event. Especially when determining the azimuth, on this occasion, as on any other, a number of us measured it independently and then we compared our measurements in order to eliminate subjective errors.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you arrived at the site, a BH television crew was already there, right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot state that explicitly. There were a number of cameras there. There were also foreigners. I don't know if there was the BH television because they didn't wear -- wear anything as to say who they were. Anyway, we had more important business to attend to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say "foreigners," are you trying to say that foreign television crews were there with their cameras when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot state that with any certainty, but it was common in such cases that -- to have cameras around, but nobody cared who they were because it was the least important thing to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll just try to have an image from Google marked. 1D1209, please. Everything is there on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is an image from Google Earth. Can you mark the position of Markale Market here?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we please zoom in a bit more?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But then we'll be unable to see all that we need to.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But just so that I can mark Markale Market.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But once you mark it, we can no longer zoom out or zoom in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it has to be saved, then. What I suggest is that we first zoom in, that the witness not yet marks anything but describes where it is. We'll then verify that. We can then zoom out again and have that portion marked. So could we please zoom in? Witness, without marking yet, do you see the Markale Market?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see the street diverging. The word "Markale" is derived from "marktplatz." There is a roofed-over part and across the street there is an open-air part, but what confuses me is this series of white dots. I don't know what they might represent, especially given that this was taken off Google earth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mean the little squares?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no squares. I mean round white dots around the building I think is Markale. White round dots encircling a building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I see that on --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we take it from the centre and if we would use clock numbering it would be approximately at 10.00, halfway from the centre to the edge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to me, this is the National Bank of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Of course, I don't know if there are any columns around that building. I guess you know that better than I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, are you able to find on this Google Earth picture where the Markale Market, whether the open market or whether the roofed market, can be found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it is this part on the left-hand side of the picture, but I'm confused by this because I have a very exact nature, since I'm a doctor of science, so it is this belt of white dots around this building, it seems unrealistic to me as far as satellite imagery is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that doesn't -- Mr. Lukic, if you want to proceed on the basis of this answer, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will leave this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will leave the topic, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll try with 1D1210.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this map, Mr. Turkusic, although it is already written there, could you just tell us for the record where Markale is here? Can you mark Markale here as well as the Svjetlost building? In the middle of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the orientation of the tram tracks where it says Markale here, that is the open air market. Opposite the tracks, a bit to the right, is the closed Markale Market which is actually Markale 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you mark it with M1 and M2, then?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: M1 would be the open air market, the marketplace, and it has to do with the case of Markale 1, well known, a well-known incident. Markale 2 drawn in this way would be approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then could you mark Svjetlost with the letter S?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, this M2 should be moved to the right because in terms of the geometry of this drawing over here where it says "taxi," that could be the market.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you like us to delete this and would you like to do it again?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is M2, as suggested by this drawing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this moment, we would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour, no objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour. Again, if there is a dispute about where the locations are, we are happy to agree with the Defence where they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Including that building which apart from Markale 1 and 2 was marked by the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, we would be happy to look into that and agree with the Defence on a location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile, Mr. Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D350.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Turkusic, and that's why we did this now, that in the Svjetlost building, the Supreme Command of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was located?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Supreme Command? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the Supreme Command was?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Actually, that is only known in peacetime. It would be absurd if one were to know in wartime where the Supreme Command is. It's not a department store.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkusic, could you then explain how you could tell us that it was not in the building Mr. Lukic referred to? Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I hesitate to object to your question but I believe the witness's response is that he did not know. In response to your question do you know, he said he did not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, first of all, it's not common to object to questions of the Judges. In our collegiality, we correct each other very nicely during breaks. But let's then -- nevertheless, apart from whether it's an objection or not, you draw my attention. The question was: "Do you know, Mr. Turkusic, and that's why we did this now, that in the Svjetlost building, the Supreme Command of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was located?" And the witness answered: "The Supreme Command? No." I understood this and so did my colleagues as an affirmation that it was not there. You may have understood the answer in a different way and you could have asked questions in re-examination on this perhaps not 100 per cent clear answer. Witness, could you now answer my question, how you would know that it was not in the Svjetlost building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In addition to the fact that it is never stated where the Supreme Command is, in "couloirs" there is often reference to where a Supreme Command is or not. However, people usually keep this in the realm of guesswork. I was not interested, but I believe that the Supreme Command was not precisely in that building. But sorry, on the same topic, the soldiers that we saw in the movie, I assert that that was no command where the soldiers went in and out because that was where the marketplace was and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is -- I asked you earlier to focus your answers on the questions. Your belief is that the Supreme Command was not in that building. Is there any fact known to you which supports that belief?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. That is just my belief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it is possible to activate a mortar shell statically and by throwing it, say, from the top of a building?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Theoretically, and practically, in terms of speculation, we can assume anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the immediate vicinity of this location, incidents had occurred earlier on in Markale, right, and in the street of Vase Miskina, in the previous period?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which incident do you mean in the Vase Miskina street?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the shelling in Vase Miskina street? I don't want to testify now.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to a street and over a million shells fell in Sarajevo and you're asking me imprecisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you work on a case when only one shell fell and caused great damage, killed a lot of people?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the bread line?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Both speakers are speaking at the same time.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about that but I didn't work on that investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you know that only one shell exploded then as well?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you deal with the possibility of, say, of static activation of the shell at Markale 2 or not?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We abhor such speculation. We did not deal with that. I beg your pardon, Your Honours, but this is insane, where the population is so dense --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking -- Mr. Lukic is not asking for your views on whether it's insane or not. The simple question was whether you have dealt with the possibility of static activation of the shell at the Markale 2 incident. Have you considered that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did not because not a single element indicated that possibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you did consider it because you excluded it, if I understand you well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I wasn't precise enough. It never crossed our minds to do that because nothing indicated that that was something that we should do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When reaching conclusions, did you rely on forensic medical findings after the victims were examined?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was not our job.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether, as far as the fatalities in this incident are concerned, whether a post-mortem had been carried out in terms of post-mortem findings or not only a post-mortem examination?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not deal with that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then I'm not going to show you some photographs of the victims because you did not deal with that. Who determined the direction from which the projectile came?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, several times by measuring it. My colleagues who were with me several times by measuring it. And then we compared our results in order to eliminate any subjective error.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that 170 degrees plus/minus 5 degrees was what you established?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was 170 plus/minus 5, as is written here. The plus/minus 5 is our subjective dissociation from possible error.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is customary?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not, because the English artilleryman just said 170, without any deviation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was a bit perplexed by this, when you say English. We heard a Frenchman here who determined the azimuth, and the French interpreters in this courtroom interpreted what he said. So which foreign force did this Englishman belong to?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of the report of an English artillery man which is very voluminous and highly based on mathematics. It had to do with the flight of the shell and he precisely calculated that angle as being 170 degrees, and that completely coincides with our findings, although we worked independently of each other. Maybe Major Higgs, if I remember correctly. Please don't take my word for it, but the Court is aware of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Soon I will have the opportunity of speaking to Mr. Higgs but I'm going to ask you whether you know that the French, who were on the spot, did some measuring and what was read was 2.850 thousandths parts, mils, which would be about 175 degrees. Did you know that that's what the French did on the spot?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that, but I'm not perplexed by that at all. I am certain of our measurements.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Attached to your report, after the explosion, together with your colleague, Nedim Bosnic you provided a map where you marked the possible trajectory of the projectile, where it had come from.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We worked on this geometry in detail, all the possible and necessary geometry. I don't know which map you refer to, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's time for our break, so we're going to take a look at that after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what we will do. We -- could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness will be brought into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I'd like to briefly discuss the plans the Prosecution has in calling Mr. Baraybar. Immediately after witness RM -- I think it was 102 or 201? The last witness of this week. Is there a fair expectation that we could conclude the testimony of that witness this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: RM21 is the next witness and then we intend to call Mr. Baraybar and then Mr. Butler. I think that with respect our estimates, we'll be able to fit that in tomorrow. I don't know with Mr. Lukic if he'll be able to complete that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, first of all, the present witness, how long do you think you would still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think I'll try to finish by the end of this day, and I really mean this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You should. There is a lot to be said --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is a lot to be said about the way in which you conducted your cross-examination. We'll not do it at this moment. Would Mr. Baraybar also be available, well, let's say Tuesday morning? Or --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the information that I have available to me right now is that Mr. Baraybar is available to give evidence next Monday, 2nd of September, and then I would have to check actually based on what I have currently available whether that would carry into Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please do so also because we might have to consider whether or not to have an extended session on Monday and that needs to be organised and we have to check whether it's possible at all. So therefore, give some further attention to your plans. Mr. Lukic, the appearance of Mr. Baraybar one week after he was originally scheduled may, I presume, cause no problems. You would have been ready for him already?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic will cross-examine Mr. Baraybar, so he is maybe more knowledgeable if there is any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honours. We will be ready for Mr. Baraybar on Monday, and it is our plan to examine him for 3 and a half hours approximately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Lukic, are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Our apologies, Witness, that we dealt with a practical matter when you entered the courtroom. We will now continue. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that now we can see P498, in the B/C/S version -- so it's document P498 we need, and it's page 18 in English and page 21 in B/C/S. Court's indulgence. Actually, the map is on page 23 in the B/C/S version and on pages 20 and 21 in the English version. But I think that it's better to use only one because there is no text anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could this one be rotated so that it takes the original position again?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the highest feature on this map? That's the summit of Trebevic, it's south of Dobra Vode, and the altitude is 1698 metres, if you can see it?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you help me with the name of the location?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Dobra Vode?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that indicated on the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's to the right of these lines.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it. Should I circle it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please, to the south there is the altitude of 1628.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see 16 but the rest is a bit blurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is it. Since you're from Sarajevo, do you agree that the terrain closer to the summit of Trebevic becomes increasingly more difficult because it's ever steeper?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can assume as much but I don't know the area that well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you draw a line under the angle of 160 degrees roughly on this map?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's rather arbitrary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, arbitrary.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the place of the impact of the shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please save this as the next Defence Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I don't stand by this because I followed your instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we want the line at 160, why not agree on where that line would be instead of asking a witness to guess approximately where it is? I mean, let's be accurate on these matters. 160 degrees is -- again --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We just give direction. Of course, we are not expecting that the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course it's slightly to the right of 170 and 165. I take it that 165 is the right of the three which are marked already, so it's -- okay, but if you think that's helpful. I would say if you want one at 160, put one on 160, then we know where we are, and not approximately, because I take it, Mr. Lukic, that you will use that later as an argument on -- from where the fire may have come. Why then not be accurate? Be precise. I agree with it -- or with the Prosecution, what exactly that line would be. Then you know where it would be and then argument later would not be influenced by this kind of lack of precision. There is no reason not to have it in evidence, I take it, but I invite the parties to put the right 160 on this, on the photocopy of this map. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The original is under seal, but I do not see many reasons if only this page would be separated from the original exhibit, that needs then to be done, and then to have this marking. Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I was -- yes, there is no reason for it to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is it uploaded as a separate or is it now part of the totality? Yes. It will be saved as a separate exhibit and the parties are invited to draw the proper 160 degrees line on this map. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D351.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 65 ter 10343 from the Prosecution list? This is the correct orientation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Turkusic, you remember that in the Milosevic case you explained how you came up with this direction of 170 degrees?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Based on these traces, you established that the angle of the explosion was 170 degrees in relation to the sidewalk?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then I misunderstood. Please explain.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see this line, the dotted line which ends before the letter C. This line represents the average centre of gravity of the shell. The azimuth is perpendicular to that line. That is the direction from which the shell flew in, and this perpendicular line represents the azimuth, whereas the angle of descent of the shell, if I remember correctly, should be the angle Alpha, and in three dimensional reality, it's the angle between the line ending with A and the wall. It is inclined, and that's the angle Alpha. That's the angle of descent of the shell. These two angles are different.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you measure whether this dotted line is parallel to the sidewalk?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is irrelevant. It's only important that this dotted line is the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat these technical details?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please slowly repeat your answer? The interpreters need some time to find the right interpretation for these technical terms. So could you restart? You said it is irrelevant and you said it is only important that the dotted line is, could you resume from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This dotted line in this photograph looks parallel to the building but that is a result of chance. It doesn't matter. It represents the line of the greatest density and the position of shrapnel traces on the ground. General -- in general terms, in relation to the impact of the shell, they have a -- they look like an arch or an eyebrow. When this line substitutes a geometrical shape, you can determine the azimuth by drawing a perpendicular line. You can see the indication that it's an angle of 90 degrees. That's how you determine the azimuth. It's a line perpendicular to line C, and the angle of descent of the shell is marked Alpha. That's an angle that indicates the inclination of line A in relation to the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I see, is the angle Alpha visible on this drawing? And where do we find it then exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this drawing, the angle Alpha is a spatial angle. If we were to look at this in 3D, that's the angle of descent of the shell, when it hit the ground, and its inclination in relation to the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was whether the angle Alpha is visible on this because this is not 3D, and therefore I take it that it's not visible, or is it indicated somewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other sketches, that angle is explicitly demonstrated, and the way it was calculated too. But it's been a number of years. It was -- I had to draw an angle Alpha in a hypothetical direction B which suggests an azimuth of 220 degrees. I believe I was requested to draw that angle too. But I considered that angle to be a hypothetical one. I don't stand by this because it isn't backed up by any measurements. I'm referring to line B now, the angle of that line is 220, as you see. That's a hypothetical azimuth that was suggested, but it wasn't me who did so. I think it was a Defence that suggested this angle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we should look for the real measured angle Alpha we should look at other parts of the documentation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, the documentation is very detailed and all our drawings are. They are geometrically very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You determined the minimum angle of descent as being 67 degrees, you remember?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's certainly the minimum angle of descent because if the shell had flown in under a smaller angle it would have hit the roof. This is the minimum possible angle of descent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have in e-court Prosecution Exhibit 10227? It would be advisable for Mr. Turkusic to have the legend on the left-hand side in order to deal with my questions, and that's on the second page, and also the sketch that is on the third page. Actually, first we are going to look at the sketch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Just for clarity of the record [Microphone not activated] --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Oh, there we go. For clarity of the record, this is in evidence as P498 and these are beginning at page 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Should I use that document, since we have this document separately introduced by the Prosecution? Whatever you would prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would prefer to have as little doubles as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Then can we have P498, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Not to be broadcast, then. [Interpretation] Sketch of the scene is two pages after this first page. [In English] If it's possible to have -- yes, thank you -- only one. And counterclockwise for 90 degrees. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Turkusic, on this sketch, can you see number 1? And does that show the place where the 120-millimetre shell fell as is stated in the legend?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what the legend says, it looks like it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On this sketch, do you see that the distance is 1.95 metres?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 2.60 is the width of the sidewalk in front of the building, right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When we add up A and B, then the distance to the wall of the building is 4.55 metres. So 1.95 plus 2.60, that is a total of 4.55?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what we see in front of us, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we zoom in? I have difficulties reading it and usually I follow on my own screen where I can zoom in, but it only gives the English version and not the B/C/S original sketch. Therefore, could we zoom in and could we then restart. Number 1 is the street, 1.95, is that 95 or 1.25? Could we -- 1.95.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, looks 1.95. And then we have the distance to the building, that's 2.60 or 2.80. 2.60.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we move it a centimetre to the right? Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there we have 2.60 again. Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I don't know whether that is also part of this large document because I used smaller documents. I have 10233.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's a 65 ter number?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since we don't have an answer, I would like to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You didn't put a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, I asked my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: It took me a little while to find the page but this is also in P498 and it's page 24 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your help. Then can we have P498, page 24? Also it's under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it's the same photograph from the document that we have already discussed. And you will see that here you can see information to the effect that the distance from the top of the building is 4 metres, 60 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that 60 or 80? How do we have to read that? Could we zoom in on -- it looks more of an 8 to me, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And I think this indicates the distance between the wall of the building and the location of the impact. And not the height of the -- no, it's -- I think it indicates the length of that arrow [overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Correct, only I -- there is some extension at the top of the building, so it seems that it's marked as from that pillar. And you are right, it's the length in between the wall and the place of impact. So when Judge Orie said 280, now I'm looking at this number that way as well, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Turkusic can you explain this to us, whether it's 4.60 or 4.80?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see 8 here because that number was written also in this triangle on the left-hand side where it says 4.80, and 11.45 is the height.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So how do you explain these differences? Over there, we saw on the sketch of the scene, the previous one, that it was marked that this was 4.55 metres from the wall and now here we have 4.80.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sketch that we are looking at now on the left and right sides, it's one and the same drawing, was made on the basis of my measurements and the measurements made by the team that was from the KDZ, from my unit. The previous sketch that we looked at was, I think, drawn by the CSB. However, in order to have correct entry data, two of our members climbed on to the top of the market and from the top to the bottom mentioned the vertical line or rather the distance from the top of the building downwards, which is 11.45. Then we also took into account the roof that was expanded. It's like the top of a hat. It's a bit wider than the building itself. That is important for the descent of the shell because in a vertical projection, that is a point that has to be covered by the shell, and then the distance of that point is relevant for drawing this triangle. That is what I did and the team from the KDZ that worked on all of these calculations; that is to say, of the smallest or rather minimum possible angle and everything that would follow. I don't want to pre-empt anything now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you coordinate your views with the CSB?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a difference like the one I've noticed just now. Obviously we did not. They made this sketch, this legend, a leg, an arm, et cetera. We saw the legend, what it describes, and I wouldn't want to go into all of these numbers because they are not the result of my measurement or of the team of the KDZ that I belonged to.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please be asked to speak slower again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I again ask you at the request of the interpreters to slow down your speed of speech.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The stabiliser you found on the scene, according to documentation, was reported to have been ejected 28.9 metres away from the place of explosion. Could the transcript also reflect that I said laterally.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to --

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you have an explanation as to how this could have happened, namely that the stabiliser would be ejected laterally to that distance?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, when we arrived, the stabiliser had already been taken by the CSB team that arrived before us. Now, whether before they arrived somebody had moved it, that is something I don't know. But it is possible. However, it is also possible that it could be ejected that far because this is what I talked about yesterday, this elastic clash. When the stabiliser impacts a very hard surface, it literally bounces off like a little ball.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it usual that it would be ejected laterally?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is nothing usual there. Every case is specific, and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness repeat the second part of his answer at a slower pace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The interpreters are asking to you repeat what you've been saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, at least the second part of the answer. You said every case is specific. And what did you then say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Every case, as far as shells are concerned, is specific. It depends on the angle, the place of impact, the firmness of the surface, the intensity of the explosion, the speed at which the shell arrives, and in this case, like in many other similar cases, it has to do with an elastic clash of the stabiliser with the hard surface, and then literally it bounces off like a tennis ball. That is characteristic of elastic clashes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to try to play a video for you. That's the video that we talked about today that we received from your colleague who actually brought it to the Tribunal and handed it over to the Tribunal. This will show two stabilisers marked during the on-site investigation by either your colleagues or the policemen, marked with numbers 12 and 13. So now I would like to ask that we start -- of course, we need cooperation between our case manager and Mr. Ram, and we would like to play it from 23:14.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before we move on to questions about this photograph, let me say that I've just been informed that in this document, P4298 [as interpreted], on page 4, it says that the explosion happened at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the time shown by the camera can deviate by three hours because the time is set up by the camera operator. So if the time was not set exactly, then that information is not reliable. It may be correct, but there is no guarantee for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your daily work, did you encounter such problems, where it was the wrong date or the wrong time set on cameras? Was it usually correct or wrong?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never used cameras in practice, but I know that when you set up the camera you set the time and date, and if that's correct, then the time stamp of any recording, any shot, is correct. If not, then that's unreliable information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, on line 6 in -- on page 44, I think the number is wrong, the P number. I think you referred to P498.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, one 2 is inserted extra, you're right, Your Honour. P498. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Turkusic, let us now focus on the document on the screen, which is 1D1224. Let me tell you that these are two stabilisers, one marked L1, the other L2. In the lower portion, we see the original photographs. In the upper portion, we see the same stabilisers, only we added a red mark where the firing pin hit the fuse so as to make it better visible. Let me tell you what this is about. These are parallel photographs of the stabilisers that are here in this Tribunal physically, and the stabilisers from the photographic documentation. The photographs are rotated, L2, in such a manner that the lines touching the tool-marks of the basic charge are parallel. That is, the position of the marks on the basic charge are unchanged. Let me immediately add that this has nothing to do with you. We are only checking something else that happened before this Tribunal. Do you agree that the imprint of the firing pin in one case touches the line, and in the other case is almost two millimetres away?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment what somebody else did, nor can I comment on the story about two stabilisers. I can't see any marks and don't know where two came from. Even more so, since the one on the right is a very good, sharp photograph, whereas on the left-hand side, the photograph is technically rather poor. And any comments of mine about what you're asking me could only amount to speculation, and I can only testify about what I know and what I'm certain about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of course, I only asked you to comment if you were in a position to do so but thank you anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, who did draw these lines on the photographs?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Our experts, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now, is this supposed, just for me to understand, to demonstrate what, more or less? That the ones here in the Tribunal are not the ones which were found?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What's in the Tribunal and what's in the photo documentation. We claim that it's not the same tail-fin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that -- that would be [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Or maybe the real one is misplaced somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just trying to look at it in a bit more detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can I use the time to put one question to the witness? I'm not so familiar with these technical details. Is it possible, if you have such a thing in your hands, to turn the middle round part of it to the right or to the left, while everything else remains in the same position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for this question. That's exactly what I wanted to comment upon.
