If I had a stabiliser in my hands and wanted to make alterations with a tool that goes into these two dimples, I could turn the central fuse which was marked red here and return it under a different angle. Since it was activated already, and it exploded, it can -- it can be taken out and returned or you can enter or insert actually another fuse. So the one who has this -- this device in his hand can manipulate it in a number of ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you another question in relation to these photographs? Do I understand that the fins of the stabiliser are changed in shape upon the impact and the forces exercised on these fins after the impact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we see all around are the fins, and they are strongly deformed. They are made of sheet metal and welded on to the body. Depending on the surface the stabiliser hits, it will deform in different ways. This shape of a stabiliser, with flattened fins, as we see here, make me believe that this stabiliser was run over by vehicles, possibly trucks, and that these vehicles flattened it. In other words, these fins, just as stabilisers of missiles, and these are these pieces of sheet metal that have a fan-like form, stabilise the shell during its flight. In other words, the stabilisers are these pieces of sheet metal around the body which are deformed. But the entire piece is also called a stabiliser because that is its function.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would the fins be regularly around the centre upon firing, upon being produced?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. These fins make sure that the shell flies regularly and prevents the shell from rotating. It doesn't change direction so that these fins actually preserve the direction of flight. They make sure that the head is in front and this tail is in the year. Talking about air-bombs, they also have fins, but such fins as keep the air-bomb in such a position that the head points to the ground and the fins point up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I wasn't asking about air-bombs. If you look at these photographs, L1 on the top, and L1 at the bottom, do you see in the deformation of these two stabiliser fins, the deformation of the fins, do you see any significant differences in the way in which they are deformed? Or would you consider them to be deformed in the same way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To me, this suggests the same kind of deformation, but I have strong reservations as to the provenance of this second piece. The igniting fuse, that is the yellow part, can be manipulated, it can be turned in any direction and change position as is being suggested here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I was not asking about that. I was asking about the deformation of the fins. Could you do the same and refrain from any further comment on the central part. The deformation of the fins of the stabiliser L2, top and bottom, do you see resemblance or do you see any significant difference in the way in which these stabiliser fins are deformed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we compare images L2, the upper and the lower one, if that's the question, I can see that the stabilisers are identical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In its deformation of the fins, is that what you -- because that's what I asked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the deformations in images L2 in the upper half and the lower half is exactly the same, as far as I'm able to tell, by looking at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may interrupt, for a second, I apologise. Those are the same, L2 and L2, upper and lower are the same. The difference is in between L1 and L2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we would have to -- and let me then see. L1, upper photograph, is the photograph taken where?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think here in the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Here in the Tribunal. L1, lower photograph, is taken where?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, L1? You asked about L1?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's from photo documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Photo documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Taken at sometime in 1995 in Sarajevo, I guess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. And now -- I'm trying to understand what we are really looking at. You say L1 is taken from the photo documentation so that's one of the pictures we will find in the exhibits, in the reports, and to be even more precise, it looks as if it is taken from photograph on page 29, hard copy, ERN number 00339229. If I'm looking at it well. Okay. So we have L1, both at the top and the bottom, taken from the -- because that seems to be the same. Now, L2 is taken where and when?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As I understood --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First, the upper one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Upper one was just the lower one with a red dot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking you where was the photograph L2 taken, under what circumstances, where and when and by whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: By our expert witnesses during the preparation for Karadzic trial here in the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And they were provided it -- with that, I'm not clear now, whether with the Registry or the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the angle under which the photograph was taken compared between L1 and L2, is that the same or is that different?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was told that they tried to make it the same. That's why the picture is rotated. Obviously the picture was taken from another angle and then they rotated the picture to have the same line going through the centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If I'm talking about an angle, I'm talking not how the camera rotates but how the camera is -- this is difficult to explain on the transcript. A camera can rotate with still being in the same surface, and you can rotate it in another way. I'm wondering whether we have precise information about the rotation of the camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What happened here, if I can explain, I cannot testify but if I can explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you cannot testify but, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Those experts were presented with L2 as being L1, and as the witness explained today, that was obviously what happened. Somebody tampered with the evidence here, and it was different from this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's see. Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He said it was easy if somebody has it in his hand to tamper it -- with it --

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- and that's the difference they noticed. That's the difference they noticed in between the photo documentation and the evidence here in the Tribunal. We want to point out to Your Honours already now that there is something wrong with the evidence kept here in the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I'd just like to put on the record that that's certainly a mischaracterisation of the witness's evidence, but I'll leave that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, where did the witness say that? I'm trying to just understand both your questions and the answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He just said that if somebody has it in his hands, it can be changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, no, no. What he said -- what he said was --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But of course he does not know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, no. What he said is, that that's at least how I understood it, that the central part can be moved, which is not the same as tampering with. It apparently is a part which is -- can be screwed in and out. Is that how I have to understand your testimony, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll be even clearer. If you look at these two dimples to the left and right of the centre part, these are the places where a tool is applied and then you can rotate this inner part which is made of brass. That's one possibility. The other is that the primer that we see in the centre contains -- which contains the fuse --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please start over?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please start again where you said that the primer that we see in the centre contains -- as you said, which contains the fuse, yes, could you resume from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In the centre there is the primer. It contains a kind of explosive which, when touched by the firing pin, activates the charge, and this -- this is a part of the missile. It can be taken out and put back again. Of course, once the shell has exploded, it is not dangerous. One more thing that I noticed by looking at these images is that these two photographs were not taken under the same angle in relation to the geometrical axis. That's the centre of the stabiliser, that's what I mean by axis. And the right -- the right-hand photograph was photographed from above that axis obliquely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, just for me to understand, the Defence's position is that the central part was taken out and then replaced by another part? Is that it? Or is it the totality of the stabiliser including the fins which is, in the position of the Defence, not the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As I understood, and I wasn't present during the examination of these pieces, of these fin tails, our experts think that it's either completely different fin tail or tampered, the original one, because it was loose and when they checked it the first time it was firm. Later on they were presented with a loose, this round shape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see: Were your experts then provided with these tail fins at several occasions?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They were in the courtroom. They were provided with it in the courtroom. It was presented. They asked for it to see it and it was presented to them in the courtroom and they noticed that something was wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But they compared it with the previous occasion where they --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Previously they were examining it with the Prosecution, Prosecutor present, just taking photos, I guess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Now, at least I understand what it's all about, what you say the stabiliser fin here in the Tribunal is either a totally different one or at least one which has been changed and perhaps the central part being changed. I can imagine that this is relevant for any numbers found on that central part. At least now I understand what the issue is, not yet what the answer to the issue is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to clarify one matter. Mr. Lukic you said L1 and L1 in the upper and the lower part of the screen are identical except the line drawn --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The red dot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And the red dot in L1 in the upper part in the middle of the fin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, red dots.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The two red dots are added.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Added.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: By the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Our experts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Defence experts. That's the only difference. Otherwise the photographs --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From the lower ones, yes, that's the only difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is what I wanted to establish for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you said the red dots from the lower ones --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, red dots are on the top ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are only on the top ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And they are added to what?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To see -- to be more clearly where that needle hit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I take it that the ones the Prosecution claims are the original ones are still available?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic. At least it's clear what the issue is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Before we do, if I could just make a few things clear for the record. The photograph that's marked as L1 is from Exhibit P499, page 29.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In hard copy? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: B/C/S version. And the video that the Defence discussed beginning at transcript, temporary transcript page 10 today, which they gave the ERN as V00047491A, that is in evidence as P446 under a different ERN, and we haven't received any ERN or other identifying number for the video that was played beginning at temporary transcript page 42. So perhaps if the Defence could provide that, that would be helpful for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As I am informed, there is no ERN for this video but the Prosecution received that video from Mr. Suljevic and you can find it in your archives, I'm sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Will it be tendered or how will it be recognised as part of the record?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will tender. We will -- actually, I forgot to ask Your Honours for that portion to be tendered. And we'll cut that portion from the original video, we'll provide the whole video to the Prosecution, if they don't have it, and I'm sure they do, and if they want to use any other parts, that's -- they would have it on their -- at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes, we would like an opportunity to review the whole video and then perhaps agree to the portions to be tendered, and I will discuss that with Mr. Lukic after court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that can be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then we will wait for the outcome of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we MFI then this portion that we played today? It's on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's on the record which portions were played, isn't it, by minutes and seconds. Could we leave it to that or if you -- then it should be uploaded separately and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will upload it separately for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Once that's done, you can -- we could already reserve a number for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to ask for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar could you reserve a number for the still to be uploaded portion of the video that was played?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that will be Exhibit D352.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and once it's uploaded the Chamber would like to be informed. Mr. Lukic, one more question. The two photographs at the right-hand side, the L2 ones, perhaps I asked it already but then I have missed the answer, when exactly were these photographs taken? And by whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I have in my handwriting, it says March 2010.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: March 2010. Under what circumstances, in the laboratories of your --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, here in the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Here in the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's 5th of March, I was just reminded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 5th of March. In the presence of whom exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know the name of the prosecutor. It's one of the prosecutor from the Karadzic team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the striking issue seems to be that the position of the central part was different in the original compared to where it is now so it may have been screwed a bit out or a bit in, but that's the real issue which is clearly visible on these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As I was told, not only that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not only that. If there is more, we will learn but that's what we focused on at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have it recorded in the Karadzic transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that's not in evidence so I would be glad to read it or if the parties could summarise it, what the issue was, I'm quite happy, but at this moment, I can't look at it, at least I expect that you would not wish me to go through other transcripts of other cases and find evidence there, and I never do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of course I don't expect that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then please make it possible for me to understand. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Turkusic, we excluded you here just now and you are our central person here today. I do apologise. I will make a correction, the film was not submitted by Mr. Suljevic. It was submitted officially by the CSB Sarajevo, the video that we watched.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Since all Prosecution videos are processed and labelled with ERNs and we don't have an ERN, we would need a copy of this directly from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will provide you with a copy, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like us to move on to those four projectiles that fell near Markale as marked before the Markale 2 incident of 28th of August, 1995, and that is paragraph 113 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In e-court, we would now need P2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, this is your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What are you looking for, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm looking for one document. I have it in front of me. I'm just -- I have one text cut out. I'm just checking whether it's from the statement or from the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it Markale 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not Markale 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No? It's about Markale 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No. It's about four projectiles fired. It's paragraph 113 and further. It should be page 32 in English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The statement is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I found it. It's from the statement. And we need paragraph 114.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mention that in your statement, in paragraph 114, you speak about a CSB report, reporting that four 120-millimetre rounds fell on the 28th of August, 1995, and that it was established that these four projectiles were fired from the southwest direction, 240 degrees, plus/minus 5 degrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You talk about paragraph 114, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The corresponding document would be P02010. If you wanted to look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had 65 ter numbers. Thank you for helping further.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question: Would you agree, even if these shells did fall on that day or any other day, is it correct that they did not come from this direction that you established, that was the direction of the shell that fell in Markale on the 28th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I directly participated in this and I stand by that as for Markale 2, the 28th of August. We continued the investigation, the CSB that had arrived beforehand. They documented that and they sent us the document, the report, or rather the findings that the azimuth was found to be 240 plus/minus 5, and to give a direct answer to your question: That angle is not the azimuth that was established in Markale 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In accordance with that, we lawyers sometimes put questions that seem illogical to experts in particular but for the record I have to ask you the following: Is it correct that these four shells, in relation to that one that was found in Markale, could not have been fired either from the same place or by the same artillery piece?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is very likely, because Sarajevo was surrounded by a great deal of artillery fortifications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that make it any more or less likely? I mean, you can fire from one place, ten shells. You can also fire one shell from ten different positions. What is the likelihood? I mean, where does -- it's based on what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Likelihood? The likelihood is very low. It is very unlikely that the shells were fired from the same place, from the same artillery piece, from the same fortification, in view of the rather significant difference in azimuth, and that is about 70 degrees. I think that it was another fortification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Time for a break, if I'm correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's time for a break so that we can think about the answer. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have a break and we will resume at 1.30. Mr. Weber you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I want to report back about Mr. Baraybar. He's also available next Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That gives us some extra air to breathe. We resume at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness is escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now get document P2009?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Turkusic, while we are waiting for the document to appear, you said that you went to the site where those four projectiles fell, right?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not certain now about the number, although can we see P2010, please. I forgot the guidance from Judge Orie, he told me it's 2010. I forgot.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Turkusic, is this the document where these four shells we discussed are dealt with? Can you confirm that this is the document that deals with the four shells?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Sarajevo Security Services Centre drafted this official report. There is a team headed by judge Asim Kanlic and other people as listed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are not mentioned as having taken part in the on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not on this team and did not go there in this manner, but later on, we went to inspect the site of impact, determine the azimuth and so on, but on that day, this had a lower priority as compared to Markale 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is there a document saying that you actually went to the site and inspected the four locations?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, because they forwarded the shell pieces to us for analysis. This must have been documented.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question is whether there is a document that you went to the site.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so. There should be one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it part of the documentation that you reviewed when the OTP prepared you for the testimony?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. There are a great many documents so I cannot be certain, but there should be. Paragraph 116 describes the case. I'm referring to my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what I found in your statement, but the document about the event doesn't mention you. That's why I'm drawing the comparison.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document on our screen is about the team headed by the investigative magistrate and the CSB, whereas paragraph 116 of my statement says that there is a document signed by Ekrem Suljevic on my behalf which means that I worked on that document and it contains my name and my initials but a colleague signed it because I was probably busy doing something else. So there must be a document of the unit to which I belonged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the document referred to in paragraph 115 and 116 is admitted as P2011. And perhaps one of the documents in there says analysis conducted by, and then for Emir Turkusic, and the other one says the same. Witness, could I ask you: These reports are mainly stating that that objects were sent for expert analysis. I could not immediately find that you went on the spot, at least in these two reports. Mr. Lukic, would you please proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Could we get 1D1221 in e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We made a table in which we tried to show that for some reason there is an irregularity in registering events and documenting them in relation to incidents. From one of your colleagues --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, is there an English version? I can't read it clearly on the screen at this moment but it seems to be B/C/S to me. There seems to be no English version of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We received the translation this morning, so it's not in the system yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you try to have it uploaded as soon as possible? Meanwhile, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the left column we see the name of the document. In column 2, the address of the -- where the incident happened. And in the third column, the log number of the document. And there is another column on the same document. Then there is a date. And another column which is grey at the top, the log number of the CSB application. Another grey column titled, "Date of CSB application." And the last column, where we entered an irregularity. And the title of the column is "Regularity of log entry." We see that number 5, that on the 26th of May, 1995, the application was made to enter an incident, which happened at Safeta Zajke 43. And in the KDZ log, it was attributed number 387, whereas, for example, document number 4 was sent on the 24th of May, 1995, whereas in the KDZ log, it was assigned number 401. There are more examples. Do you have an explanation how it happened that documents and applications sent later were assigned a smaller number?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For something to be irregular, we must first define what is regular. Since this is the only example in the history of warfare that such analyses have ever been made, and individual impacts have been investigated into, in the hierarchy of the state MUP, of which I was part, and the local MUPs which request us to do -- which submit requests for services; that is, to analyse some parts or go to a site. In keeping logs, assigning numbers, entering dates and so on, it would be very surprising if there were -- if there were no incongruences, considering the large number of cases that we processed parallelly, simultaneously, or subsequently following requests by the Sarajevo CSB. However, the documents that we kept, I believe, are very accurate and we tried to keep as many or as much physical evidence as possible, and the greatest mistake that we may have made is one that has to do with dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who assigned which number and determined the sequence of entering incidents?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any document that was drafted was assigned a number higher than the previous document by one. When the number of cases were analysed simultaneously, it would have been strange if there hadn't been errors. However, there was a war on, and we are now looking at documents as if this had been peacetime and you had one case a week. It was the other way around. We had seven cases per day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you know how your documents were registered at the CSB?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They send us a request bearing a number. We attach our number, depending on the sequence of cases. We forward that to them, and then they enter that under a number of their own, depending on the system they use for archiving.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you don't know what kind of system they used?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. It's difficult to describe a wartime situation to someone who wasn't in such a situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 117 of your statement and that is the first paragraph in chapter 22, entitled, "Additional comments chart" --

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- you comment on the document that is now 65 ter 10145. It also has a P number, and that's 1100. You speak about Cobanija Street and the 18th of June, 1995, but we see that it's the 16th of June, we can tell from the associated document, but I suppose that is a typographical error.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is why I would like to see P933 from e-court. For the time being, I'm interested in the upper photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this place as being Cobanija?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a long time ago. There were many details, pictures, sketches, so I'd have to refresh my memory along with some additional information about what I see in this photograph now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were thousands of similar cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us briefly look at P1100, then. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a typical document that we write, and we always write the subject, that is to say what we are working in connection with, and here we have a CSB document number 19/04, et cetera, et cetera. It is described what we were asked to do, what was submitted to us. Afterwards our analysis follows and our opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember the Cobanija 7 case now?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. We have this photo documentation accompanying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P933 is what I'd like to return to now, P933. [In English] And we need page 2 in B/C/S, since those are pictures. We need the lower picture to be zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Turkusic, in this photograph, it is evident that this pipe down here and the one up there is not damaged, and it is being claimed that an air-bomb had exploded. Could you please explain that to us?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please show me the second page of that document in B/C/S that I looked at a moment ago? Actually, the first page and the second page. And then we are going to look at the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we please take a look at P1100?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I was going to suggest I can provide a hard copy to the witness if we want to leave the photograph on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then we can leave the photo on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you saw the document. Now, is it correct?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You stated that it was an air-bomb.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where does it say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So in the opinion, page 2, it says that it is Grad 122-millimetres, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One rocket engine, Grad 122-millimetres, cannot in any way propel an air-bomb, so it is not correct that what is written here is an air-bomb. However, it can propel a smaller projectile, and this would be an improvised device basically. So one rocket engine. Air-bombs were made with four or five rocket engines.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here in the report from the scene, which is an attachment to this document, it says --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We don't have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Cobanija number 7, on the 16th of June, 1995, 1710, a projectile fell and exploded in Cobanija number 7. It was of highly destructive power, and the heating room was fully destroyed, like -- as were five privately owned cars and a garage. So, in your view --

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was it that exploded?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's described here, first of all, when using a rocket engine for propelling a projectile, it leaves one of its parts with the fins that were not opened because its purpose is completely different. And here, on the scene, a trace was found, or, rather, parts just of one rocket engine. It had to be a smaller explosive bombshell, less destructive and less explosive than an air-bomb that weighs several hundred kilograms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Now let us briefly look at P933, page 6 in e-court. This is the damage that was established on the garages. Also, let us look at page 4. Damage was established here as well, in the garages. Now let us briefly take a look at a sketch, 1D1218.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Does it all pertain to the same case?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This sketch, would it correspond to -- actually, we did this. Would it correspond to the scene where we see the heating plant, the garage, the awning, and the walls and also the point of impact on the heating plant?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know on the basis of what you drew this sketch, because the description would have to be very detailed in order to provide the dimensions, whereas here we have several things drawn with ideal geometric proportions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, where does this come from? Is there an English version of this sketch?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we drew it just to try to summarise. I anticipated I wouldn't have much time. I just wanted to ask the witness which grenade could hit the pink building and destroy the yellow garage, when we know that the grey area is ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I object to that question particularly based on this drawing which the Defence has drawn. As the witness noted, we have no idea what the dimensions are, what the point of view was, or how this corresponds to the underlying documents, what kind of a reconstruction it was of the investigative file. We just simply don't have enough information for a foundation for that kind of response from the witness, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it's also for the Chamber rather difficult to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- interpret or to understand any answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I had many pictures from the photo documentation, I don't have time now, I promised to finish today. I would just ask something in relation to these rockets.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you agree, Mr. Turkusic, that on the 17th of April, 1992, an attack was launched against the Pretis factory by the TO of the BH and that on that occasion, several truck loads of rockets were taken out, and that is why this date is commemorated as a significant date in BH?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. We took our own rockets. These are hand-held rocket launchers, the calibre is a bit bigger and they are intended for the destruction of tanks and APCs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the photo documentation for this incident, we have 65 ter 10294. We need page 4.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's a one-page document, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what I understood. Can we see P933, page 9?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need the lower photograph. Do you know which one of these parts was found in the garage?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but it looks like a rocket system, propulsion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to the documentation, it was the part in the middle that was supposed to have been found there.

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's the provenance of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Prosecution -- actually, this is a Prosecution exhibit, and this is part of the photo documentation that they received from Sarajevo in relation to this incident. However, we are coming to the end so I'm just going to ask you the following: Grad 122-millimetres, that it is assumed -- now I'm going to ask you whether you would agree that not a single one of these parts belongs nor can it belong to a Grad 122-millimetres?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree. From the point of view of what we state in our report, because we had many cases of analysing the remains of a Grad rocket, and this is a part that is deformed to a relatively low degree, and it can be recognised after an explosion. What is of larger calibre, that is of a larger calibre than those used by hand-held rocket launchers, if that is what you are getting at.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's not what I'm getting at. I just asked you whether any one of these parts we see in the photograph can belong to the Grad 122-millimetres?

utterances.speaker: EMIR TURKUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of what I remember, I cannot recognise any one of these parts with full certainty, but I'm absolutely sure that when we wrote the report and when we analysed the parts, we concluded that this was one Grad rocket and that that is what propelled it. It was that rocket. Or, rather, its engine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have concluded my examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Ms. Harbour could you give us an indication as to how much time, if any at all, you would need for re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I will try to keep it short, Your Honours, and hopefully no more than ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is understood. Witness, we would like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 for further questions. It may not take very long tomorrow. I again instruct you that you should not speak or communicate with whomever about your testimony, even not the small portion still to be given tomorrow. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile Mr. Lukic, the Prosecution has informed the Chamber, and you as well, that the complete investigation file for the 18th of June incident, Simon Bolivar school was uploaded and requests the completed file to replace the existing content of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, since we introduced photo documentation that was missing from the Prosecutor's file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's P2043. Hereby, the evidence now in P2043 may be replaced and the registry is accordingly instructed to replace it by what is now doc ID 0033-4855 and a translation, same number with the extension et. Nothing else? Ms. Harbour?

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: We've requested, and we do request your leave as well, to bring in the Markale 2 mortar stabiliser into the courtroom. And that's artifact A001-3855. And it's 65 ter 22925 in our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then we can have a look at it. Nothing else? Then we adjourn for the day and we'll resume tomorrow, Friday, the 30th of August, 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom, III.
